```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.6, fig.align = "center")
library(tidyverse); library(scales); library(plotly); library(knitr)
asu_maroon <- "#8C1D40"; asu_gold <- "#FFC627"; grey_dark <- "#5C6670"

raw <- read_csv("Chicago_Energy_Benchmarking_20261029.csv",
                col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE)

energy <- raw %>%
  rename(year = `Data Year`, id = ID, status = `Reporting Status`,
         community_area = `Community Area`, property_type = `Primary Property Type`,
         gfa = `Gross Floor Area - Buildings (sq ft)`, year_built = `Year Built`,
         elec_kbtu = `Electricity Use (kBtu)`, gas_kbtu = `Natural Gas Use (kBtu)`,
         steam_kbtu = `District Steam Use (kBtu)`, site_eui = `Site EUI (kBtu/sq ft)`,
         wn_site_eui = `Weather Normalized Site EUI (kBtu/sq ft)`,
         ghg = `Total GHG Emissions (Metric Tons CO2e)`,
         ghg_intensity = `GHG Intensity (kg CO2e/sq ft)`) %>%
  select(year, id, status, community_area, property_type, gfa, year_built,
         elec_kbtu, gas_kbtu, steam_kbtu, site_eui, wn_site_eui, ghg, ghg_intensity) %>%
  mutate(across(c(year, id, gfa, year_built, elec_kbtu, gas_kbtu, steam_kbtu,
                  site_eui, wn_site_eui, ghg, ghg_intensity), parse_number)) %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(status %in% c("Submitted", "Submitted Data") ~ "Submitted", TRUE ~ status),
         property_type = replace_na(property_type, "Unknown"),
         year_built = if_else(year_built < 1800 | year_built > year, NA_real_, year_built),
         era = cut(year_built, breaks = c(0, 1900, 1945, 1975, 2000, Inf),
                   labels = c("1900 & earlier", "1901-1945", "1946-1975", "1976-2000", "After 2000")))

analysis <- energy %>%
  filter(status == "Submitted", !is.na(site_eui), site_eui > 0, site_eui <= 500,
         !is.na(gfa), gfa > 0)

yearly <- analysis %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(median_eui = median(site_eui), median_ghgi = median(ghg_intensity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
get_y <- function(col, yr) yearly[[col]][yearly$year == yr]
```

## The question

**Chicago's big buildings must report their energy use every year. Are they actually getting more efficient?**

* Data: Chicago Energy Benchmarking, City of Chicago Data Portal (`r comma(nrow(energy))` building-year records, 2014-2023)
* Main measure: **Site EUI** = energy used per square foot per year
* Four questions:
    1. Is the improvement real?
    2. Do older buildings waste more energy?
    3. Did COVID change energy use, and did it last?
    4. Which property types drive emissions?

## Cleaning: what I fixed and why

* Numbers were stored as **text with commas**, so I converted them
* "Submitted" vs "Submitted Data" labels differ in 2020 and 2022, so I merged them (otherwise two years vanish)
* Neighborhood names had **inconsistent capitalization**, so I standardized them
* Extreme EUI values (up to **15,634**) were removed above 500 (`r comma(sum(energy$status == "Submitted" & energy$site_eui > 500, na.rm = TRUE))` records)
* Created new variables: construction **era**, fuel **gas share**, size groups, COVID **period**
* Final analysis set: **`r comma(nrow(analysis))`** submitted building-years

## Q1: Median energy intensity fell, mostly in a step in 2020

```{r q1}
ggplot(yearly, aes(year, median_eui)) +
  geom_line(colour = asu_maroon, linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(colour = asu_maroon, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2023) +
  labs(x = "Data year", y = "Median site EUI (kBtu per sq ft)",
       title = "Median site EUI by year") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15)
```

## Q1: The same buildings improved too

```{r q1b}
panel <- analysis %>% filter(year %in% c(2016, 2023)) %>%
  select(id, year, site_eui) %>% group_by(id, year) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = year, values_from = site_eui, names_prefix = "eui_") %>%
  drop_na(eui_2016, eui_2023) %>% mutate(improved = eui_2023 < eui_2016)

ggplot(panel, aes(eui_2016, eui_2023, colour = improved)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = asu_maroon, "FALSE" = "grey60"), name = "Improved") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 250), ylim = c(0, 250)) +
  labs(x = "Site EUI 2016", y = "Site EUI 2023",
       title = paste0(percent(mean(panel$improved), accuracy = 1), " of ", comma(nrow(panel)),
                      " buildings improved")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15)
```

## Q1: Emissions fell even faster than energy use

* Median energy intensity, 2019 to 2023: **`r percent(get_y("median_eui", 2023) / get_y("median_eui", 2019) - 1, accuracy = 0.1)`**
* Median GHG intensity, 2019 to 2023: **`r percent(get_y("median_ghgi", 2023) / get_y("median_ghgi", 2019) - 1, accuracy = 0.1)`**
* Likely reason: a **cleaner electricity grid** (a hypothesis, not tested in this dataset)
* Takeaway: some emissions progress is not something building owners did

## Q2: Age is not a simple story

```{r q2}
analysis %>% filter(!is.na(era)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(era, site_eui, fill = era)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "text", aes(label = round(after_stat(y), 0)),
               vjust = -0.8, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#F2D7A0", "#E9B84F", asu_maroon, "#C4622D", grey_dark)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 220)) +
  labs(x = "Era built", y = "Site EUI (kBtu per sq ft)",
       title = "Mid-century (1946-1975) buildings are the energy hogs") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15)
```

## Q3: COVID hit property types very differently

```{r q3, fig.height=4.4}
major_types <- c("Office", "Hotel", "College/University", "Retail Store", "K-12 School", "Multifamily Housing")
covid <- analysis %>% filter(property_type %in% major_types, year >= 2016) %>%
  group_by(property_type, year) %>% summarise(med = median(site_eui), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(property_type) %>% mutate(index = 100 * med / med[year == 2019]) %>% ungroup()

ggplot(covid, aes(factor(year), property_type, fill = index)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = round(index, 0)), fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2E7D9A", mid = "white", high = asu_maroon, midpoint = 100,
                       name = "2019 = 100") +
  labs(x = "Data year", y = NULL, title = "Offices dropped about 20% and never came back") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Q4: A few property types punch above their weight

```{r q4}
shares <- analysis %>% filter(year == 2023, !is.na(ghg), ghg >= 0) %>%
  group_by(property_type) %>%
  summarise(buildings = n(), floor_area = sum(gfa), emissions = sum(ghg), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(c(buildings, floor_area, emissions), ~ .x / sum(.x))) %>%
  slice_max(emissions, n = 5) %>%
  pivot_longer(-property_type, names_to = "measure", values_to = "share") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = c("buildings", "floor_area", "emissions"),
                          labels = c("Share of buildings", "Share of floor area", "Share of emissions")),
         property_type = fct_reorder(str_wrap(property_type, 18), share, .fun = max))

ggplot(shares, aes(property_type, share, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", asu_gold, asu_maroon), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of reporting buildings (2023)",
       title = "Hospitals: tiny share of buildings, large share of emissions") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Interactive map

```{r map, fig.height=5}
map_df <- analysis %>% filter(year == 2023) %>%
  left_join(raw %>% transmute(id = parse_number(ID), year = parse_number(`Data Year`),
                              lat = parse_number(Latitude), lon = parse_number(Longitude),
                              property_name = `Property Name`),
            by = c("id", "year")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), lat > 41.6, lat < 42.1, lon > -88, lon < -87.5) %>%
  mutate(eui_capped = pmin(site_eui, 200),
         tip = paste0(coalesce(property_name, "Unnamed building"), "<br>", property_type,
                      "<br>EUI: ", round(site_eui, 1)))
p <- ggplot(map_df, aes(lon, lat, colour = eui_capped, text = tip)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, name = "Site EUI") +
  coord_fixed(1.3) + labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

## Conclusions

* **Real progress, with caveats:** the same buildings improved, but much of the drop arrives as a 2020 step
* **Age is U-shaped:** mid-century buildings are the best retrofit target
* **Not every drop is efficiency:** half-empty offices use less energy per sq ft
* **Emissions are concentrated:** prioritize by emissions, not building count
* **Electrification** matters most for older housing and schools (gas heavy)
* Limitations: only reporting buildings, COVID confounding, grid effect is a hypothesis

## Thank you! Questions?

*If you ever find yourself in a half-empty Loop office building in January, remember: it is still heated, and it still shows up in the data.*
